top_story: Since 11 July, the crisis has moved from a reported U.S. strike and Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz into a broader campaign, with Washington carrying out a third straight night of attacks by 13 July and preparing to enforce a maritime blockade on all Iranian ports and oil terminals from Tuesday. Trump’s announcement of a Hormuz blockade, including charges for safe passage, pushes beyond military retaliation into coercive control of one of the world’s most critical shipping lanes, raising immediate risks for Gulf energy flows, commercial shipping, and civilian livelihoods tied to imported fuel and food. His stated intent to strike Iran’s hardened Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site signals that the operation is widening from maritime pressure to strategic infrastructure. The trajectory now points toward a longer conflict that couples direct U.S. force with economic strangulation, increasing the chance of regional disruption far beyond Iran’s coastline.
